descriptions.after: The Attachment the beam ends at.

descriptions.before: Scales the light emitted from Beam when LightInfluence is 0.

descriptions.before: Determines the color of the Beam across its segments.
descriptions.after: Determines the color of the beam across its Segments.

descriptions.before: Determines, along with Beam.Attachment0 the position of the first control point in the beam's Bézier curve.
descriptions.after: Determines, along with Attachment0, the position of the second control point in the beam's Bézier curve.

descriptions.before: Determines, along with Beam.Attachment1 the position of the second control point in the beam's Bézier curve.
descriptions.after: Determines, along with Attachment1, the position of the third control point in the beam's Bézier curve.

descriptions.before: Determines whether the Beam is visible or not.
descriptions.after: Determines whether the beam is visible or not.

descriptions.before: Determines whether the Beam.Segments of the Beam will always face the camera regardless of its orientation.
descriptions.after: Determines whether the Segments of the beam will always face the camera, regardless of its orientation.

descriptions.before: Determines to what degree the colors of the Beam are blended with the colors behind it.
descriptions.after: Determines to what degree the colors of the beam are blended with the colors behind it.

descriptions.before: Determines the degree to which the Beam is influenced by the environment's lighting.
descriptions.after: Determines the degree to which the beam is influenced by the environment's lighting.

descriptions.before: Sets how many straight segments the Beam is made up of.
descriptions.after: Sets how many straight segments the beam is made up of.

descriptions.before: The content ID of the texture to be displayed on the Beam.
descriptions.after: The content ID of the texture to be displayed on the beam.

descriptions.before: Sets the length of the Beam texture if Beam.TextureMode is 'Wrap' or 'Static'. If Beam.TextureMode is 'Stretch' then it determines the size of the texture relative to the Beam's length.
descriptions.after: Sets the length of the beam's texture, dependent on TextureMode.

descriptions.before: Determines the manner in which the Beam.Texture scales and repeats.
descriptions.after: Determines the manner in which the Texture scales and repeats.

descriptions.before: Determines the speed at which the Beam.Texture image moves along the Beam.
descriptions.after: Determines the speed at which the Texture image moves along the beam.

descriptions.before: Determines the transparency of the Beam across its segments.
descriptions.after: Determines the transparency of the beam across its segments.

descriptions.before: The width in studs of the Beam at its base.
descriptions.after: The width of the beam at its origin (Attachment0), in studs.

descriptions.before: The width in studs of the Beam at its end.
descriptions.after: The width of the beam at its end (Attachment1), in studs.

descriptions.before: The distance, in studs, the Beam display is offset by relative to the Workspace.CurrentCamera.
descriptions.after: The distance, in studs, the beam display is offset relative to the CurrentCamera.

descriptions.before: Overrides the default selection adornment (used for gamepads).
descriptions.after: Overrides the default selection adornment used for gamepads.

descriptions.before: JointInstance is the base class for joints, such as Connectors, Welds, and Snaps.
descriptions.after: The base class for joints.

descriptions.before: Truss parts are the same as Parts, except that they have a different visual style, resize differently and characters are able to climb them.
descriptions.after: Similar to a Part but with a different visual Style and the important distinction that default characters are able to climb it.

descriptions.before: Sets what the truss looks like. There are currently three different styles.
descriptions.after: Sets what the truss looks like.

descriptions.before: Determines the distance in studs by which studio's drag and move tools move objects each tick.
descriptions.after: Determines the distance in studs by which Studio's drag and move tools move objects each tick.

descriptions.before: Determines the degrees by which studio's rotation tool will rotate selected objects each tick.
descriptions.after: Determines the degrees by which Studio's rotation tool will rotate selected objects each tick.

descriptions.before: Determines whether studio tools will use local space of an object or global space.
descriptions.after: Determines whether Studio tools will use local space of an object or global space.

descriptions.before: Returns the studio user's userId if they're logged in, otherwise returns 0.
descriptions.after: Returns the Studio user's userId if they're logged in, otherwise returns 0.

descriptions.before: The Trail object is used to create a trail like effect between two points.
descriptions.after: Used to create a trail effect between two attachments.

descriptions.before: Determines where the Trail will start drawing its segments.
descriptions.after: Along with Attachment1, determines where the trail will start drawing its segments.

descriptions.before: Determines where the Trail will start drawing its segments.
descriptions.after: Along with Attachment0, determines where the trail will start drawing its segments.

descriptions.before: Scales the light emitted from Trail when LightInfluence is 0.
descriptions.after: Scales the light emitted from the trail when LightInfluence is less than 1.

descriptions.before: The color of the trail segments throughout the lifetime of the trail.
descriptions.after: The color of the trail throughout its lifetime.

descriptions.before: Toggles whether the trail will be drawn or not.
descriptions.after: Determines whether the trail will be drawn or not.

descriptions.before: Whether the trail textures will always face the camera.
descriptions.after: Determines whether the trail will always face the camera, regardless of its orientation.

descriptions.before: Duration of the trail in seconds.
descriptions.after: Determines how long each segment in a trail will last, in seconds.

descriptions.before: Sets how much the colors of the trail are blended with the colors behind them.
descriptions.after: Determines to what degree the colors of the trail are blended with the colors behind it.

descriptions.before: Determines the factor to which the Trail is influenced by the environment's lighting.
descriptions.after: Determines the degree to which the trail is influenced by the environment's lighting.

descriptions.before: Minimum length of a trail's segment in studs.
descriptions.after: Sets the minimum length of the trail.

descriptions.before: The texture to display on the trail.
descriptions.after: The content ID of the texture to be displayed on the trail.

descriptions.before: Sets length of texture if Trail.TextureMode is Wrap or Static. If mode is Stretch sets number of times texture will repeat.
descriptions.after: Sets the length of the trail's texture, dependent on TextureMode.

descriptions.before: Sets how Trail.Texture will be drawn.
descriptions.after: Determines the manner in which the Texture scales, repeats, and moves along with the trail's attachments.

descriptions.before: Sets the transparency of the Trail's segments over the trail's Trail.Lifetime.
descriptions.after: Sets the transparency of the trail's segments over its Lifetime.

descriptions.before: A NumberSequence that scales the width of the Trail over the course of its lifetime.
descriptions.after: Scales the width of the trail over the course of its lifetime.

descriptions.before: The texture will be stretched out based on the lifetime of the trail, and will shrink inwards if the trail stops moving.
descriptions.after: For a Trail, the texture will stretch out based on the lifetime of the trail, and shrink inwards if the trail's attachments stop moving. For a Beam, the texture will repeat TextureLength times across the beam's overall length. See here for details.

descriptions.before: The texture will be tiled as the length of the trail changes, but the textures will remain stationary relative to their attachments.
descriptions.after: For a Trail, the texture will be tiled as the length of the trail changes, but the textures will remain stationary relative to their attachments. For a Beam, the texture repetitions will equal the beam's overall length (in studs) divided by its TextureLength. See here for details.

descriptions.before: The texture will be rolled out as the attachments move, and they will remain in place until their lifetime is met.
descriptions.after: For a Trail, the texture will be rolled out as the attachments move, and they will remain in place until their lifetime is met. This setting is ideal for trail textures that should appear "stamped" where rendered, such as paw prints or tire tracks. This value is not supported for Beam and therefore behaves identically to Wrap.
